correctness.rationale: The full overlap graph is balanced and reaches the all-zero root by repeated zero appends. Its outgoing choices are forced at weight two. Suppressing those choices sends a one-one position j to j+1 (or the root) by appending zero, and to s−1−j by appending one, for s=k−1. A reflected choice at j≥floor(s/2) traps [s−1−j,j], including the possible central self-loop. Otherwise all selected paths strictly advance and reach the root. The root's unique outgoing edge fixes rotation, and the BEST factorial product is 1 because every degree is at most two. The last-exit construction is a bijection here: at a nonroot degree-two vertex the chosen last edge fixes the full order. The factor set has k+C(k,2) distinct labels, giving the stated length. A fresh unused-window search at k=3–10 matches the quoted counts, confirms every low-position last-exit vector occurs once and verifies the k=5 example up to rotation. Exhaustion in these cases corroborates the unbounded argument rather than replacing it.
residual_risks: The classification pertains to rotation classes, not reversal or complement; the low positions are counted from the right.

evidence: Fredricksen says there is a twofold attachment choice for each weight-two rotation coset, except the even-length antipodal coset with one attachment, giving 2^floor((k−1)/2). For the bridge, on the ≤2 overlap graph use rotation as the default successor. Any Euler tour is a successor permutation obtained by switches of the two outgoing images at the zero vertex or a weight-one vertex. The zero loop has to attach. Each weight-two necklace must attach to the weight-one necklace at least once. The two possible attachment slots at one-one indices j and k−2−j are paired by complementary separation, with a single slot at the antipodal center. Do one switch for every necklace first, obtaining a single cycle with each weight-two necklace inserted at the chosen slot of the main weight-one cycle. If a necklace were switched twice, its remaining switch joins two endpoints in this cyclic order located at its two paired slots, one endpoint in the inserted segment. All such endpoint pairs are nested or disjoint in the main cycle's order. Switches at distinct vertices commute, and noncrossing pairs split current cycles without rejoining: after a split all remaining endpoint pairs lie within one component or the other. Thus a single cycle admits no doubled switch, so every tour is in exactly the counted subclass. In the canonical traversal starting from the zero root, a low-index vertex appends 1 on its last exit exactly when its necklace attaches at the paired high index (if attached at low index it appends 1 on the first pass and 0 on returning).

originality.rationale: Fredricksen (1993) explicitly gives the same numerical formula and the same independent paired-position join choices for binary weight at most two in its minimum-density subclass. The scope qualifier matters: the paper excludes split-and-rejoin constructions in general. For this t=2 specialization all candidate choices reduce to switches at pairs with nested positions, so the apparently wider possible class contributes no extra cycles, as witnessed below. The frozen last-exit representation recodes the same paired choices; its alternative proof does not establish a distinct claimed count or structural degree of freedom.
